detail:
The National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH) lists the adult attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder studies conducted by its intramural research program at the NIH Clinical Center in Bethesda, Maryland. The studies described on the page focus on young adults, including outpatient research on compulsivity in young adults ages 18 to 30 and parallel research on impulsivity in the same age group, both examining links between those traits, genetics, and the brain.

NIMH describes participation in these studies as symptom-based, with parts that can be done remotely and parts conducted at the NIH Clinical Center. Participants in the studies described receive a detailed assessment and clinical feedback. NIMH presents the work as part of its intramural effort to understand how traits central to ADHD and related conditions vary across people and relate to brain function and genetics.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about ADHD research and clinical trials.
summary: NIMH lists its intramural adult ADHD studies, including outpatient research in young adults on compulsivity and impulsivity and their links to genetics and the brain, conducted partly remotely and partly at the NIH Clinical Center.
takeaways: nimh adult adhd studies described focus on young adults
researchers study impulsivity and compulsivity, genetics, and the brain
research participation is optional; talk to your doctor about studies
title: ADHD: where ADHD research is heading
